abstract: ArXiv:2607.09254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study matrix feasibility problems "find X in K intersect C" where K is a closed convex matrix set and C = {X : sigma(X) in S} is defined by a convex constraint S on the ordered singular values. Using the classical spectral transfer identity, projection onto C reduces to an SVD plus a small quadratic program. For seven natural polyhedral S we embed this projector in a plain alternating projection (AP) loop. We experiment with two concrete families of K - linear constraints (an affine subspace intersected with an entrywise box) and ellipsoidal constraints (a non-centered anisotropic Frobenius ellipsoid) - although the method applies equally to more general convex constraints. The experiments expose three regimes: rapid feasibility, slow tail convergence, or informative infeasibility plateaus.
tldr: This paper studies matrix feasibility problems with spectral constraints using alternating projections.
motivation: To solve feasibility problems where a matrix must satisfy both convex constraints and constraints on its singular values.
method: Reduces projection onto the spectral constraint set via SVD and a quadratic program, then applies alternating projection for two families of convex sets.
result: Experiments reveal three regimes: rapid feasibility, slow tail convergence, or infeasibility plateaus.
conclusion: The method is effective for certain problems but may suffer from slow convergence or infeasibility detection issues.

title: Low-Complexity Successive-Cancellation List Decoding Of $2\times2$ Kernel Non-Binary Polar Codes
authors: Pingping Chen Xinyu Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-binary successive cancellation list (NB-SCL) decoding expands each surviving path into [MATH] candidate branches at every information symbol, which causes high path expansion, sorting, and pruning complexity. To address this issue, this paper proposes low-complexity list decoding algorithms for [MATH] kernel non-binary polar codes (NBPCs). First, we design a split-reduced non-binary successive cancellation list (SR-NBSCL) decoder that skips path splitting when the current symbol is sufficiently reliable. We then exploit the final Rate-1 node structure and switch the last group of information symbols to simplified non-binary successive cancellation (NB-SC) decoding, resulting in the enhanced split-reduced non-binary successive cancellation list (ESR-NBSCL) decoder. To further reduce branch expansion at unreliable symbols, we introduce an accumulated reliability-deviation (ARD) metric and propose an adaptive branch-pruning non-binary successive cancellation list (ABP-NBSCL) decoder, which prunes unreliable candidate branches before sorting and then reduces the dominant sorting complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed decoders achieve frame-error-rate (FER) performance close to that of conventional NB-SCL decoding with much lower complexity. In particular, the ABP-NBSCL decoder reduces the path splitting number (PSN) by more than [MATH] at several tested signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), with a negligible performance loss.
tldr: This paper proposes low-complexity list decoding algorithms for non-binary polar codes, focusing on reducing path expansion and sorting complexity.
motivation: Non-binary successive cancellation list decoding suffers from high complexity due to path splitting and sorting at every information symbol.
method: The authors design split-reduced, enhanced split-reduced, and adaptive branch-pruning non-binary successive cancellation list decoders that skip splitting for reliable symbols, exploit Rate-1 nodes, and prune unreliable branches before sorting.
result: The proposed decoders achieve frame-error-rate performance close to conventional NB-SCL decoding with significantly lower complexity, e.g., reducing path splitting number by over 90% at certain SNRs.
conclusion: The algorithms offer efficient decoding for non-binary polar codes with minimal performance loss, suitable for practical implementations.

title: On The Abundance Of Phase Transitions In Dynamical Systems
authors: Alexander Arbieto, Walter Britto, Elias Rego
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the mechanisms that trigger phase transitions in both discrete-time and continuous-time dynamical systems. We prove a simple topological condition that implies the existence of H\"older continuous potentials displaying phase transitions. As a consequence, we show that phase transitions are typical in several scenarios. Specifically, for [MATH] diffeomorphisms and [MATH] vector fields, we show that phase transitions are generic among non-transitive systems. In low dimensions, we conclude that they are generic for non-Anosov systems. Finally, in the [MATH] setting, we prove that on any compact topological manifold of dimension different from 4, there exists a dense set of homeomorphisms with finite entropy that display phase transitions.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in dynamical systems from a topological and ergodic theory perspective, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the mechanisms that trigger phase transitions in discrete and continuous dynamical systems, and to show that such transitions are abundant under mild conditions.
method: They prove a topological condition that guarantees the existence of Hölder continuous potentials exhibiting phase transitions, and use generic properties of diffeomorphisms and vector fields.
result: Phase transitions are generic among non-transitive systems and non-Anosov systems in low dimensions; in the C0 setting, they are dense on manifolds of dimension ≠ 4.
conclusion: Phase transitions are typical in many dynamical systems, but the work is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Near-optimal Node-private Community Estimation In Polynomial-time
authors: Laurentiu Marchis, Olga Klopp, Po-Ling Loh, Ilias Zadik
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we resolve an open question of Klopp & Zadik (2026) by providing a high-probability polynomial-time, node-private algorithm which nearly matches the performance of their exponential-time node-private algorithm for exact recovery in stochastic block models. Our result involves an explicitly constructed Lipschitz surrogate for the penalized likelihood function, as well as a carefully devised accept-reject algorithm that samples community labels from the corresponding exponential mechanism in polynomial-time. We rigorously analyze the privacy, runtime, and utility of our proposed algorithm, showing that even when the number of communities K grows logarithmically with the number of nodes n, we can achieve the minimax rates for exact recovery with the privacy parameter epsilon growing as log(n), thus matching known lower bounds on the cost of privacy for this setting.
tldr: This paper provides a polynomial-time node-private algorithm for community detection in stochastic block models, achieving near-optimal exact recovery.
motivation: The goal is to design a computationally efficient algorithm for community estimation under node-level differential privacy, resolving an open question from prior work.
method: The authors construct a Lipschitz surrogate for the penalized likelihood function and use an accept-reject algorithm to sample community labels from the exponential mechanism in polynomial time.
result: The algorithm matches minimax rates for exact recovery with privacy parameter epsilon growing as log(n), even when the number of communities grows logarithmically with n.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that near-optimal node-private community estimation is achievable in polynomial time, closing the gap between exponential-time and polynomial-time algorithms.

title: Portable Acceleration Of Learning With Errors KEMs For Post-Quantum Cryptography
authors: Tiziana Liberati, Nitin Shukla, Simone Rizzo, Elisabetta Boella, Matteo Barbieri, Gabriella Bettonte, Daniele Gregori, Marco Pedicini
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is driving demand for implementations that can meet the computational requirements of real-world applications. Among the proposed PQC constructions, Learning With Errors (LWE) based key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs) are particularly attractive due to their strong security foundations, but they incur substantial computational costs from matrix operations and large-scale cryptographically secure random number generation. These characteristics position GPU acceleration as an effective approach for lowering the computational overhead of lattice based cryptographic schemes. In this work, we present a portable GPU implementation of a plain LWE based KEM using OpenMP Target offloading. Unlike most existing GPU implementations, which rely on CUDA specific optimizations, our approach uses a single source code base that executes on both NVIDIA and AMD accelerators. We evaluate the proposed implementation on different accelerator architectures, analyzing performance benchmarking, runtime profiling, scalability analysis, and energy to solution measurements. Experimental results show that OpenMP Target offloading delivers substantial acceleration over a multicore CPU baseline while preserving source level portability across heterogeneous GPU ecosystems. Cross platform analysis identifies NVIDIA GH200 and AMD MI300X as the most effective platforms for this memory bound workload, while profiling indicates that memory system organization and CPU GPU interaction play a more critical role than peak compute capability alone. These findings demonstrate that portable GPU acceleration can significantly reduce the computational overhead of PQC while avoiding vendor lock in, thereby facilitating the deployment of quantum resistant cryptographic infrastructures.
tldr: This paper presents a portable GPU implementation of a Learning With Errors based key encapsulation mechanism using OpenMP Target offloading, targeting post-quantum cryptography.
motivation: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) implementations need to be computationally efficient for real-world deployment, and GPU acceleration can reduce overhead while avoiding vendor lock-in.
method: The authors implement a plain LWE-based KEM using OpenMP Target offloading to run on both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs from a single codebase, and benchmark performance, scalability, and energy consumption.
result: OpenMP Target offloading achieves substantial acceleration over multicore CPU baselines, with NVIDIA GH200 and AMD MI300X being the most effective platforms; memory organization and CPU-GPU interaction are critical factors.
conclusion: Portable GPU acceleration can significantly reduce computational overhead of PQC while maintaining cross-platform portability, facilitating deployment of quantum-resistant cryptographic infrastructures.

title: On The Gaussian-Quadratic Rate-Distortion Function For Vector Sources With Individual Distortion Constraints
authors: Shuao Chen, Junyuan Gao, Yuxuan Shi, Yongpeng Wu, Giuseppe Caire, H. Vincent Poor, Wenjun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the Gaussian-quadratic lossy compression with arbitrary source length under individual distortion constraints. The rate-distortion function (RDF) is lower-bounded by a Hadamard inequality-based rate, which is tight if and only if the semidefinite condition (SDC) holds. Otherwise, this bound becomes loose, and analytical results are lacking. Moreover, the fundamental quantitative relationship between source correlations and the RDF remains incomplete. In this paper, we provide new theoretical results under different source covariance matrices and distortion constraints. First, under arbitrary covariance and distortion constraints, we obtain the spectral properties of the optimal source reconstruction achieving the RDF, and a stronger scalar inequality version of the SDC. We propose a class of source covariance matrices based on hierarchical correlations and show that studying the two-type correlation (2-TC) model is sufficient to establish the analytical foundation for the broader class. Under this covariance, we obtain the RDF with source correlations explicitly incorporated when the SDC holds, and analyze the SDC from the perspectives of distortion constraints and source correlations. Next, under the 2-TC covariance and two-type distortion (2-TD) constraints, we establish the complete RDFs over seven regions on a distortion plane, with the optimal distortion (rate) allocations determined in each region. It is revealed that the essence of pursuing the complete RDF lies in thoroughly analyzing the correlations between the optimal distortions. Finally, under isotropic correlation and identical constraints, we provide the per-component compression rate and show that exploiting correlations can significantly reduce compression costs.
tldr: This paper studies the Gaussian-quadratic rate-distortion function for vector sources with individual distortion constraints, focusing on source correlations and optimal reconstruction.
motivation: The rate-distortion function under individual distortion constraints is not fully understood, especially when the Hadamard inequality bound is loose and source correlations are involved.
method: The authors derive spectral properties of the optimal reconstruction, propose a hierarchical correlation model, and analyze the rate-distortion function under two-type correlation and distortion constraints.
result: Complete rate-distortion functions are established over seven regions on a distortion plane for the two-type model, and per-component compression rates are provided for isotropic correlations.
conclusion: Exploiting source correlations can significantly reduce compression costs, and the analysis of optimal distortion correlations is key to obtaining the complete rate-distortion function.

title: Density Evolution Of Soft-Decision Collapsed Projection-Aggregation Decoding For Reed-Muller Codes Over The Biawgn Channel
authors: Jiajie Li, Marvin R\"ubenacke, Warren J. Gross
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reed-Muller (RM) codes have been shown to achieve capacity over a range of channels, and recently proposed projection-aggregation (PA) decoding has been experimentally shown to achieve near-maximum-likelihood decoding performance. These recent achievements motivate theoretical research on PA decoding. In this work, we analyze the density function of the soft output from collapsed projection-aggregation (CPA) decoding for RM codes over the binary-input additive white Gaussian noise (BIAWGN) channel. We prove that soft-decision CPA decoding returns an exact marginal probability and is symmetric. Based on the analysis, we build a density evolution model for CPA decoding. To simplify the density evolution, we approximate the projection and the fast Hadamard transform decoding using hard-decision decoding. Simulation results over the BIAWGN channel show that our proposed density evolution model captures the fast reduction in the mean and the variance of the soft information returned from the CPA decoding, which qualitatively explains the decoding mechanism and the fast convergence speed of the CPA decoding. We perform an asymptotic analysis based on the proposed density evolution, and we show that CPA decoding can achieve a vanishing error probability for RM codes with a vanishing code rate.
tldr: This paper analyzes density evolution for soft-decision collapsed projection-aggregation decoding of Reed-Muller codes over the BIAWGN channel.
motivation: Reed-Muller codes have shown capacity-achieving performance, and projection-aggregation decoding achieves near-ML performance, motivating theoretical analysis of its decoding mechanism.
method: The authors prove that soft-decision CPA decoding returns exact marginal probabilities and is symmetric, then build a density evolution model using hard-decision approximations for projection and fast Hadamard transform decoding.
result: The density evolution model captures the fast reduction in mean and variance of soft information, explaining the fast convergence of CPA decoding; asymptotic analysis shows vanishing error probability for RM codes with vanishing code rate.
conclusion: The proposed density evolution model provides theoretical insight into CPA decoding performance and convergence speed.

title: Llm For Eda In Front-End Design: Challenges And Opportunities
authors: Kangwei Xu, Bing Li, Ulf Schlichtmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As chip complexity increases and time-to-market pressures grow, front-end design has become a critical bottleneck in chip development. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown great potential in Electronic Design Automation (EDA). Beyond specification understanding, LLMs show the potential to serve as a unified intelligent interface for hardware description language (HDL) generation, testbench construction, and design space exploration. The rise of agentic AI, represented by pioneering systems such as OpenClaw, offers a strategic roadmap for the next generation EDA. From this perspective, this paper discusses the evolution of EDA from localized assistance to autonomous agentic execution. Then, we review representative advances of LLMs in front-end design, focusing on key tasks such as circuit and testbench generation from a shared specification, as well as design quality improvement in established workflows such as high-level synthesis. Finally, we discuss the key challenges and limitations of integrating LLMs into EDA, and outline future opportunities for advancing LLM-enabled front-end design, offering a systematic perspective for researchers interested in leveraging agentic AI technologies for EDA.
tldr: This paper surveys the use of LLMs in front-end EDA tasks, focusing on HDL generation, testbench construction, and design space exploration.
motivation: Chip front-end design is a bottleneck; LLMs offer potential to automate and improve these tasks.
method: The paper reviews recent advances and discusses the evolution from localized assistance to autonomous agentic execution.
result: LLMs show promise in circuit and testbench generation, but face challenges in reliability and integration.
conclusion: LLM-enabled EDA is an emerging area with opportunities for agentic AI, but significant challenges remain.

title: Matched Generators For The Karhunen--Lo\`eve Transform: A Double-Commutator Eigenvalue Theory
authors: Mitchell A. Thornton
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Karhunen--Lo\`eve transform (KLT) diagonalizes the covariance of a second-order process and is optimal for mean-square truncation. Which classical transform it reduces to is governed by the symmetry commutant of the covariance: when the kernel commutes with a group action, the KLT eigenfunctions are the irreducible representation functions of that group, recovering the Fourier, cosine, Mellin, and spherical-harmonic systems. We study the inverse question. Given a covariance [MATH] and a finite-dimensional space of candidate generators, the generator nearest to commuting with [MATH], the minimizer of [MATH], is the smallest-eigenvalue solution of a double-commutator eigenvalue problem [MATH], a Hermitian generalized eigenvalue problem of size the number of generators, independent of dimension. The framework recovers hidden transforms as well as classical ones: a variational characterization turns the existence of a commuting generator into a spectral condition, and a tridiagonal commutant-uniqueness result yields the prolate spheroidal, cosine, and discrete orthogonal-polynomial bases as exact recoveries, with matrix-valued extensions, and produces a continuum of transforms interpolating between and beyond the classical families. When symmetry is approximate, the coding penalty of the symmetry-adapted blockwise transform equals the multi-information among the sectors, an exact threshold between the fixed and data-driven transforms. We further give a graph-automorphism characterization of permutation structure, a sequential deflation for non-Abelian symmetry, and stability bounds under estimation error. As an application, the KLT of a two-paradigm covariance is synthesized from its two known generators, without forming the mixed covariance, reaching the full-data transform's compaction from few observations.
tldr: This paper develops a double-commutator eigenvalue theory to find generators that approximately commute with a given covariance matrix, enabling the recovery and interpolation of classical transforms like Fourier and cosine.
motivation: The Karhunen-Loève transform (KLT) is optimal for data compression but often lacks a fast algorithm; the authors aim to find a transform that approximates the KLT while retaining a fast implementation via a commuting generator.
method: They formulate a double-commutator eigenvalue problem whose smallest eigenvalue yields the generator closest to commuting with the covariance, and analyze the spectral conditions for exact recovery of known transforms.
result: The framework recovers classical transforms (e.g., prolate spheroidal, cosine) and produces a continuum of interpolating transforms; the coding penalty of using a symmetry-adapted blockwise transform equals the multi-information among sectors.
conclusion: The double-commutator approach provides a principled way to design fast approximate KLTs and reveals connections between symmetry, commutativity, and optimal transforms.

title: Adaptive Bayes Exactly Tracks Information Over Intrinsic Time
authors: Akshay Balsubramani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayesian and multiplicative-weights updates reweight experts, models, or actions from sequential feedback. We show that the regret of any such update obeys an exact information-accounting identity. On each round, the learner's excess loss to any chosen comparator is the sum of an immediate payment for the uncertainty exposed by the round and a reduction in the information distance from the learner's current weights to the comparator. The cumulative payment defines a pathwise uncertainty clock, the of the realized sequence. Summing one-step balances yields two exact adaptive decompositions of cumulative regret, one for each natural way of composing the update across rounds. Because the decompositions are exact rather than upper bounds, favorable stochastic or low-noise regimes appear as self-bounding properties of the realized intrinsic time, not as slack in worst-case analyses. The same calculus covers Hedge, optimistic and side-information variants, continuous priors, boosting, online convex optimization, contextual bandits, and repeated games: the pathwise account is the same in every case.
tldr: This paper derives an exact information-accounting identity for Bayesian and multiplicative-weights updates, showing that regret decomposes into an immediate uncertainty payment and a reduction in information distance.
motivation: To understand the fundamental structure of online learning algorithms beyond worst-case bounds, and to provide a pathwise analysis that captures favorable stochastic regimes.
method: The authors prove an exact identity for the regret of any Bayesian or multiplicative-weights update, decomposing it into a cumulative uncertainty payment (intrinsic time) and a change in information distance to a comparator.
result: The regret equals the sum of an immediate payment for uncertainty exposed each round plus a reduction in information distance; this holds exactly for various algorithms including Hedge, optimistic variants, and contextual bandits.
conclusion: The exact decomposition reveals that favorable regimes appear as self-bounding properties of intrinsic time, not as slack in worst-case analyses, unifying many online learning algorithms under a single information-theoretic framework.

title: Polynomial Binary Optimization
authors: Endre Boros
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a binary polynomial optimization problem (BPO, in short) we are maximizing a multilinear polynomial expression depending on n binary variables. This is a hard optimization class, containing many NP-hard problems, including unconstrained quadratic binary optimization. Several tractable special classes were considered in the literature, including problems with bounded tree-width (Crama, Hansen, Jaumard, 1990), Berge-acyclic problems (Buchheim, Crama, and Heck, 2019), [MATH]-acyclic problems (Del Pia and Di Gregorio, 2022, 2023), limited reach problems (Clausen, Crama, Lusby, Rodr\'iguez, and Ropke, 2024), and [MATH]-acyclic problems with bounded rank (Del Pia and Khajavirad, 2025). We focus on a general variable elimination scheme for BPO, and develop the unique explicit multi-linear polynomial form for the equivalent BPO problem obtained after the elimination of a given subset of the variables. The obtained closed form representation of such an equivalent BPO problem allows us to characterize new special classes for which this elimination method, when applied recursively, provides a computationally efficient solution. Our approach is elementary1, algebraic, and provides efficient solution to a wide problem class that properly generalizes all of the above mentioned tractable special cases.
tldr: This paper studies polynomial binary optimization, a combinatorial optimization problem, and proposes a variable elimination scheme for tractable subclasses.
motivation: Binary polynomial optimization is NP-hard, and identifying tractable subclasses is important for practical applications.
method: The authors develop a closed-form representation of the multilinear polynomial after eliminating a subset of variables, enabling efficient recursive elimination for certain problem classes.
result: The proposed method generalizes several known tractable classes, including those with bounded tree-width and acyclic structures.
conclusion: The work provides a unified algebraic approach to solving a wide class of binary polynomial optimization problems efficiently.

title: Brownian Bridge For Coherent State Path Integral Monte Carlo
authors: Riccardo Fantoni
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new Brownian bridge construction for our newly devised Coherent States Path Integral Monte Carlo algorithm. We apply it to the numerically exact calculation of the thermodynamic properties of the Helium fluid on a plane at low non zero temperature. We find very good agreement with the conventional plane waves path integral Monte Carlo results.
tags: coherent state path integral Monte Carlo
tldr: This paper proposes a Brownian bridge construction for coherent state path integral Monte Carlo to compute thermodynamic properties of helium fluid.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and accuracy of path integral Monte Carlo simulations for quantum fluids using coherent states.
method: A new Brownian bridge algorithm is developed within the coherent state path integral Monte Carlo framework.
result: The method yields very good agreement with conventional plane wave path integral Monte Carlo results for helium fluid at low temperature.
conclusion: The proposed Brownian bridge construction is a valid and accurate approach for simulating quantum fluids with coherent states.
keywords: coherent state path integral Monte Carlo

title: The Scales Of Disorder In Perfect Quasicrystals
authors: Alan Rodrigo Mendoza Sosa, Atahualpa S. Kraemer, Michael Schmiedeberg, Erdal C. O\u{g}uz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical dichotomy between crystalline order and amorphous disorder is increasingly challenged by novel states that lack conventional crystalline symmetries while retaining crystal-like properties. Quasicrystals occupy a distinctive position within this expanding framework by possessing long-range order without translational periodicity, thereby permitting arbitrary [MATH]-fold rotational symmetry. Paradoxically, far from their unique symmetry center, high-symmetry quasicrystals closely resemble disordered patterns, raising the question of how deterministic order can be detected. Here we show that increasing rotational symmetry progressively suppresses local statistical signatures of quasiperiodicity, while preserving its underlying exact long-range order. This order is thus concealed below an emergent crossover length that grows linearly with [MATH]. Therefore, as [MATH], the disorder-like regime expands without bound, defining a symmetry-controlled geometric critical point at which deterministic order and randomness become statistically indistinguishable over any finite observation window. For finite [MATH], however, quasiperiodic order becomes detectable beyond this crossover, revealing a second emergent length scale that we identify as the size of a -- finite patches over which statistical properties recur despite the absence of conventional translational periodicity. In one dimension, the statistical-unit-cell size coincides with the crossover length, whereas in two dimensions it grows as [MATH], remaining smaller than the size of typical approximants and establishing a hierarchy of emergent length scales. Together, the disorder-to-order crossover and statistical unit cells provide a quantitative framework connecting crystals, quasicrystals, and amorphous matter, showing how apparent disorder can emerge from purely deterministic geometry.
tldr: This paper studies how increasing rotational symmetry in perfect quasicrystals suppresses local statistical signatures of quasiperiodicity, leading to an emergent crossover length beyond which deterministic order becomes indistinguishable from disorder.
motivation: Quasicrystals possess long-range order without translational periodicity, yet high-symmetry quasicrystals resemble disordered patterns, raising the question of how deterministic order can be detected.
method: The authors analyze the statistical properties of quasicrystals as a function of rotational symmetry, identifying a crossover length that scales linearly with the symmetry order, and define a statistical-unit-cell size that characterizes recurrence of statistical properties.
result: They show that as rotational symmetry increases, the disorder-like regime expands without bound, defining a symmetry-controlled geometric critical point where order and randomness become statistically indistinguishable over any finite observation window.
conclusion: The findings provide a quantitative framework connecting crystals, quasicrystals, and amorphous matter, showing how apparent disorder can emerge from purely deterministic geometry.

title: The Statistical Physics Of Unsaturated Soil Water: Kinetic Theory And Non Commutative Pore Water Dynamics
authors: Riccardo Rigon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a statistical-mechanical theory of water in unsaturated soil whose outcome is a continuum field equation for the pore-occupancy g(r,x,t), the fraction of pores of radius r that are water-filled at position x and time t. The theory is built across three scales: microscopic inter-pore transfers set by Hagen-Poiseuille rates and a driving potential (the difference of pore-class chemical potentials, taken in capillary-gravitational form but open to adsorptive, osmotic, or thermal refinement); a mesoscale master equation relaxing the occupancy toward the equilibrium step g_eq=H(r*-r); and, on contracting the averaging volume to a point, the continuum balance d_t g + div F = C[g] - E - T, of which everything else is a limit, a moment, or a boundary resolution. The kinetic equation is an Onsager gradient flow descending the Gibbs free energy, with an H-theorem for the isothermal unforced system and mass conservation as its zeroth moment. A single dimensionless group, the pore-resolved Damkohler number Da(r,x), organizes the behavior and unifies phenomenologies long modelled separately. A Chapman-Enskog reduction identifies Richards' equation as the quasi-static (Da->0) limit, with matric potential and hydraulic conductivity K emerging only there and K vanishing below the percolation threshold; capillary-bundle and critical-path models are its diagonal and spectral limits. Hysteresis is the holonomy of a forcing bundle, a geometric phase rather than per-pore bistability, with a falsifiable loop-area law H ~ I^2. Preferential flow is what the same equation does where Da>1, so the Richards/preferential-flow dichotomy becomes a continuous Da-controlled crossover. Out of the quasi-static limit g(r) is the irreducible state variable. All inputs are geometric properties of the pore network, measurable from micro-CT and calibrated against no macroscopic data.
tldr: Develops a statistical-mechanical theory of water in unsaturated soil, deriving a continuum field equation for pore occupancy.
motivation: To provide a unified theoretical framework for unsaturated soil water dynamics that bridges microscopic pore-scale physics and macroscopic continuum models.
method: Builds a kinetic theory across three scales: microscopic inter-pore transfers, mesoscale master equation, and continuum balance equation, using Onsager gradient flow and Chapman-Enskog reduction.
result: Derives Richards' equation as a quasi-static limit, identifies hysteresis as a geometric phase, and shows preferential flow as a Damkohler-number-controlled crossover.
conclusion: The theory unifies various phenomenological models of unsaturated flow and provides a falsifiable framework based on pore network geometry.

title: Intrinsic Redundancy And Local Robustness In Finite $\beta$-Expansion Systems
authors: Miras Seilkhan Adilbek Taizhanov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Redundancy in non-standard numeration systems is often associated with robustness, but its practical value in finite digital arithmetic depends on how representation, storage, and repair are defined. We study intrinsic redundancy in finite beta-expansion systems using a bounded-window model that separates semantic non-uniqueness from canonical codebook admissibility. The model distinguishes arithmetic canonicalization from corruption repair and evaluates structural detectability, value-preserving repair of the observed state, and survival of the original value. For the golden-ratio system and related multinacci bases, we prove that a genuine single-digit corruption in a canonically injective finite codebook cannot be semantically recovered by exact repair without external information. Semantic survival under exact structural repair is possible only for localized multi-digit perturbations corresponding to algebraic rewrite identities, such as the equivalence of 100 and 011. Experiments comparing standard binary, signed-digit non-adjacent form, and multinacci systems quantify trade-offs among codebook sparsity, fault visibility, canonicalization cost, residual error, and boundary loss. The results show that intrinsic beta-redundancy is a constrained-language resource for structural digital integrity rather than a substitute for classical error-control redundancy.
tldr: This paper studies redundancy in non-standard numeration systems (beta-expansions) using a bounded-window model, focusing on structural digital integrity rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the practical value of intrinsic redundancy in finite beta-expansion systems for digital arithmetic, particularly regarding representation, storage, and repair.
method: The authors propose a bounded-window model that separates semantic non-uniqueness from canonical codebook admissibility, and analyze structural detectability, value-preserving repair, and survival of original value under single-digit corruptions.
result: For golden-ratio and multinacci bases, single-digit corruption in a canonically injective codebook cannot be semantically recovered without external information; semantic survival is only possible for localized multi-digit perturbations corresponding to algebraic rewrite identities.
conclusion: Intrinsic beta-redundancy is a constrained-language resource for structural digital integrity, not a substitute for classical error-control redundancy.

title: Geometric Planted Matchings In High Dimensions: The Power Of Multiple Views
authors: Timothy L. H. Wee, Kaylee Y. Yang, Zhou Fan, Cheng Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of recovering the correspondence between a collection of [MATH] points in [MATH] and a noisy, permuted version of those points. In the high-dimensional regime [MATH], under a Gaussian model with noise variance [MATH], prior work identifies [MATH] as the threshold for almost exact recovery. We prove that this threshold is all-or-nothing: for every fixed [MATH], no estimator recovers a positive fraction of the matching, and even estimating the matched point cloud in Euclidean distance is asymptotically no better than ignoring the correspondence. On the other hand, we consider a multi-view generalization of the problem where [MATH] noisy, independently permuted copies of the same latent point cloud are observed. Here we show that a simple polynomial-time procedure recovers all relative matchings up to [MATH] errors whenever [MATH]. Thus multiple views can break the impossibility barrier [MATH] for the original matching problem: in particular, for [MATH], the two-view model has no nontrivial recovery, but a third view makes all latent correspondences efficiently recoverable.
tldr: This paper studies the problem of recovering correspondences between noisy, permuted point clouds in high dimensions, and shows that multiple views can break the impossibility barrier for matching.
motivation: The problem of matching two point clouds under unknown permutation and noise is fundamental in statistics and machine learning, with applications in computer vision and data integration.
method: The authors analyze a Gaussian model with noise variance σ², prove an all-or-nothing threshold for single-view recovery, and propose a polynomial-time procedure for multi-view matching.
result: For a single view, no estimator can recover a positive fraction of the matching when σ² > 1. For multiple views, the procedure recovers all relative matchings up to o(1) errors whenever σ² < 1 + 1/(m-1) for m views.
conclusion: Multiple views can overcome the fundamental limitation of single-view matching, enabling efficient recovery even when individual views are too noisy.

title: Tests For Increasing Convex Ordering Based On Generalized Tsallis Entropy Measures
authors: Aritra Saha, Siddhartha Chakraborty, Md. Zafar Anis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study several incomplete entropy measures, namely the Incomplete Weighted Cumulative Residual Entropy, the Incomplete Cumulative Residual Tsallis Entropy and its weighted version, and introduce the associated partial orderings. Their connections with certain well-known stochastic orderings are also investigated. Based on these characterizations, a class of nonparametric tests for stochastic equality against ordered alternatives is developed. The asymptotic properties of the proposed tests are derived, while their finite-sample performances are assessed through extensive Monte Carlo simulations under various alternative models and sample sizes. These tests are further compared with the test based on incomplete cumulative residual entropy proposed by Zardasht (2015).
tldr: This paper develops nonparametric tests for increasing convex ordering using generalized Tsallis entropy measures.
motivation: To provide statistical tests for stochastic ordering based on entropy measures, extending existing work on cumulative residual entropy.
method: The authors introduce incomplete weighted cumulative residual entropy and incomplete cumulative residual Tsallis entropy, derive associated partial orderings, and propose a class of nonparametric tests. Asymptotic properties are derived and finite-sample performance is evaluated via Monte Carlo simulations.
result: The proposed tests are shown to be consistent and outperform the existing test based on incomplete cumulative residual entropy in certain scenarios.
conclusion: The new entropy-based tests offer a useful tool for detecting increasing convex ordering in data.

title: Breaking Local-Minimum Traps In Spiking Neural Network-Based Solvers For CSPs Via Parallel Tempering
authors: Recep Bugra Uludag, Ahmet Efe, Ismail Akturk, Ulya R. Karpuzcu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) with stochastic neurons can solve constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) by encoding constraints via connectivity and performing probabilistic search via spike dynamics. However, fixed-temperature stochastic dynamics often get trapped in local minima - near-satisfying configurations - a vulnerability that escalates with problem difficulty. To overcome this, we integrate parallel tempering (PT) into the neural sampling solver, running multiple parallel replicas at varying inverse temperatures. Replicas periodically exchange temperatures rather than network states, managing the trade-off between exploration and concentration around low-energy configurations while preserving asynchronous, spike-based computation. We evaluate this architecture against a parallel baseline of four independent, fixed-temperature solvers using equal computational resources across 1000 instances from the SATLIB uf20-91 benchmark. Parallel tempering improves success probability on 332 instances while worsening only 5. Crucially, these gains are concentrated on hard instances where independent solvers fail. Violation trajectory analysis confirms the underlying mechanism: temperature exchanges allow replicas to traverse energy barriers unreachable by fixed-temperature dynamics, successfully escaping the narrow basins that constrain the baseline. To our knowledge, this represents the first integration of parallel tempering into an SNN-based CSP solver.
tldr: This paper integrates parallel tempering into spiking neural network-based solvers for constraint satisfaction problems to escape local minima.
motivation: Fixed-temperature stochastic dynamics in SNN-based CSP solvers often get trapped in local minima, especially for hard instances.
method: The authors run multiple parallel replicas at varying inverse temperatures and periodically exchange temperatures between replicas, preserving asynchronous spike-based computation.
result: On the SATLIB uf20-91 benchmark, parallel tempering improves success probability on 332 out of 1000 instances while worsening only 5, with gains concentrated on hard instances.
conclusion: Temperature exchanges allow replicas to traverse energy barriers unreachable by fixed-temperature dynamics, successfully escaping local minima.

title: Federated Learning Architecture: Data Privacy And System Security Approaches
authors: Cagdas Karatas, Hibanur Karadogan, Ahmet Yasin Ertug, Busra Buyuktanir, Kazim Yildiz, Gozde Karatas Baydogmus
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study explores the integration of homomorphic encryption and differential privacy techniques to enhance data privacy and security in Federated Learning (FL) systems. FL allows data to remain on local devices, eliminating the need for centralized data collection; however, sensitive information may still be leaked during model updates. To address this issue, homomorphic encryption enables computations on encrypted data, while differential privacy prevents the extraction of individual information through statistical techniques applied to model outputs. The proposed architecture was tested on the Framingham, Pima Indians Diabetes, and Bank Marketing datasets, revealing that enhanced privacy can be achieved without significantly compromising model accuracy. Furthermore, the impact of data heterogeneity among clients on model performance was analyzed, and it was concluded that strategies such as the careful selection of differential privacy parameters and training settings, along with the use of larger datasets, can improve the efficiency of FL. The findings demonstrate that privacy-preserving and high-performance artificial intelligence systems can be securely applied in sensitive domains such as healthcare and finance.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated learning architecture combining homomorphic encryption and differential privacy to enhance data privacy and security.
motivation: Federated learning still risks leaking sensitive information from model updates; the authors aim to mitigate this by integrating privacy-preserving techniques.
method: The architecture uses homomorphic encryption for computations on encrypted data and differential privacy to prevent individual information extraction, tested on three datasets.
result: Enhanced privacy is achieved without significantly compromising model accuracy; data heterogeneity impacts performance, but careful parameter selection and larger datasets improve efficiency.
conclusion: Privacy-preserving and high-performance AI systems can be securely applied in sensitive domains like healthcare and finance.

title: SolarChain-Eval: A Physics-Constrained Benchmark For Trustworthy Economic Agents In Decentralized Energy Markets
authors: Shilin Ou, Yifan Xu, Luyao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08681v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As agentic AI systems are increasingly applied to cyber-physical environments, their evaluation requires assessment of both task performance and trustworthiness. In decentralized energy markets, autonomous agents may improve market utility, but may also exploit invalid physical data, create artificial liquidity, and produce unstable governance decisions. Therefore, we propose SolarChain-Eval, a physics-constrained benchmark for evaluating trustworthy economic agents. It formulates market governance as a Gymnasium-compatible Markov Decision Process, where agents make hourly decisions. SolarChain-Eval evaluates each policy across multiple dimensions, including market utility, physical safety, slippage, action smoothness, spatial fairness, and auditability. To support agentic evaluation, SolarChain-Eval incorporates an LLM-based Planner/Auditor layer. The Planner defines episode-level action bounds and audit rules, while the Auditor reviews and revises high-risk actions. All interventions are recorded through structured logs, including trigger signals, proposed actions, revised actions, and audit rationales. Experiments with static, random, myopic, RL, and RL+LLM policies reveal a clear utility-safety trade-off. RL agents improve market utility but can still produce unsafe behavior. When the physics penalty is removed, reward-maximizing agents exploit invalid generation and increase artificial liquidity. The LLM Planner/Auditor improves auditability and mitigates selected risks, but it cannot fully compensate for a misspecified reward function. These results indicate that trustworthy agentic AI evaluation requires both physical constraints and transparent intervention traces. We release data and code as open access on GitHub for replicability.
tldr: A benchmark for evaluating trustworthy economic agents in decentralized energy markets using physics constraints and LLM-based auditing.
motivation: Autonomous agents in decentralized energy markets may exploit invalid data or create artificial liquidity, so a benchmark is needed to evaluate both task performance and trustworthiness.
method: The benchmark formulates market governance as a Markov Decision Process, includes an LLM-based Planner/Auditor layer, and evaluates policies across dimensions like market utility, physical safety, and auditability.
result: Experiments show a utility-safety trade-off; RL agents improve utility but can produce unsafe behavior, and the LLM Planner/Auditor mitigates some risks but cannot fully compensate for misspecified reward functions.
conclusion: Trustworthy agentic AI evaluation requires both physical constraints and transparent intervention traces.

title: A Unified Approach To Interpreting Knowledge Distillation For Large Language Models Via Interactions
authors: Qingzhuo Wang, Ruiyang Qin, Zhenxin Qin, Wen Shen, Zhihua Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite the success of knowledge distillation (KD) in Large Language Models (LLMs), the underlying mechanism behind its efficacy remains unclear. In this paper, we propose a unified approach to explore the common mechanism of various KD methods using interactions. Specifically, we decompose the output score of the LLM into the sum of numerous interactions. Each interaction represents a nonlinear relationship involving a set of input variables (e.g., words). Based on the decomposed interactions, we discover that the common mechanism underlying various KD methods is the sparsification of interactions, i.e., student models retain fewer interactions for inference while suppressing other interactions to zero effects. Furthermore, we discover that the performance variance across different KD methods arises from their capabilities in handling complex interactions. A KD method typically yields better performance if it enables the student model to achieve higher sparsity of complex interactions. Motivated by these insights, we propose a plug-and-play loss function called Complex Interaction Penalty (CIP) to explicitly enforce the sparsity of complex interactions during the distillation process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that integrating CIP consistently improves the performance of diverse KD methods on both in-domain and out-of-distribution benchmarks.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified approach to interpret knowledge distillation in large language models using interactions, and introduces a loss function to improve distillation performance.
motivation: The mechanism behind knowledge distillation in LLMs is unclear; the authors aim to uncover a common mechanism across different KD methods.
method: They decompose the output score into interactions representing nonlinear relationships among input variables, and propose a Complex Interaction Penalty (CIP) loss to enforce sparsity of complex interactions.
result: Experiments show that CIP consistently improves performance of various KD methods on in-domain and out-of-distribution benchmarks.
conclusion: The common mechanism of KD is sparsification of interactions, and explicitly enforcing sparsity of complex interactions enhances distillation.

title: Sequential Multi-Step Nanoimprint Lithography Fabrication Of Zero-Mode Waveguide Nanoaperture Arrays To Enhance Single Molecule Fluorescence Detection
authors: Hamza Khelidj, Badre Kerzabi, Igor Ozerov, Olivier Hector, David Grosso, J\'er\^ome Wenger
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-mode waveguides (ZMWs) enable single-molecule fluorescence detection at micromolar concentrations by confining light to nanoscale volumes, overcoming the diffraction limit of confocal microscopy. However, their widespread adoption is hindered by high fabrication costs and limited throughput of traditional methods like focused ion beam or electron-beam lithography. Here, we introduce a scalable cost-effective approach using sequential nanoimprint lithography (NIL) combined with hydrofluoric acid etching to fabricate ZMW arrays with tunable diameters from a single initial master. In our sequential nanoimprint approach, each stamped NIL output serves as a master for the next nanoimprint generation. By leveraging the shrinkage of sol-gel nanopatterns during annealing, we achieve a cumulative diameter reduction from 230 nm to 115 nm over four successive imprints, all based on the same initial master. The resulting ZMWs exhibit detection volumes reduced by up to 1000-fold and fluorescence enhancement exceeding 16x, achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art focused ion beam-fabricated devices. Eliminating the need for multiple master structures significantly expands the scalability of nanoimprint lithography approaches. By lowering the nanofabrication barriers and making ZMW arrays more accessible, the sequential NIL method paves the way towards broader adoption of nanophotonic devices in single-molecule biophysics, biosensing, and surface patterning applications.
tldr: This paper presents a scalable nanoimprint lithography method to fabricate zero-mode waveguide arrays for single-molecule fluorescence detection.
motivation: Zero-mode waveguides enable single-molecule detection at high concentrations but are costly to fabricate; the authors aim to reduce cost and increase throughput.
method: Sequential nanoimprint lithography using sol-gel shrinkage to reduce aperture diameter from 230 nm to 115 nm over four generations.
result: Detection volumes reduced up to 1000-fold and fluorescence enhancement exceeding 16x, comparable to focused ion beam devices.
conclusion: The sequential NIL method lowers fabrication barriers and makes ZMW arrays more accessible for biophysics and biosensing.

title: Co-design Approach To Aperture Masking For Imaging Through Atmospheric Turbulence
authors: Olivier Herscovici-Schiller, Laurent M. Mugnier, Alice Fontbonne, Pauline Trouv\'e-Peloux, Fr\'ed\'eric Champagnat, Yann Lucas, Yann Lai-Tim, Fr\'ed\'eric Cassaing
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aperture masking interferometry is a technique originally designed to alleviate the influence of atmospheric turbulence on images recorded on ground-based telescopes. In this communication, we explore the optimization of the aperture mask by an optical/digital co-design approach in order to obtain diffraction-limited images of relatively bright objects imaged through turbulence. We show that, with a few simplifying assumptions, it is possible to express the Mean Square Error of the restored image as a function of the chosen mask, of the spatial Power Spectral Density of the observed object and of the noise level, without actually computing any image. This allows us to optimize the aperture mask with a reduced computing cost. We also implement a multi-frame myopic algorithm to estimate jointly the observed object, the piston and the tip-tilt in front of each sub-aperture, and check by simulations that the aperture masks obtained indeed allow a satisfactory image reconstruction.
tldr: This paper presents an optical/digital co-design approach to optimize aperture masks for imaging through atmospheric turbulence, aiming to achieve diffraction-limited images.
motivation: Atmospheric turbulence degrades images from ground-based telescopes; aperture masking interferometry can mitigate this, but mask design is typically heuristic. The authors aim to optimize the mask using a co-design approach.
method: The mean square error of the restored image is expressed as a function of the mask, object power spectral density, and noise level, enabling optimization without full image computation. A multi-frame myopic algorithm jointly estimates the object and wavefront aberrations.
result: Simulations show that the optimized aperture masks enable satisfactory image reconstruction.
conclusion: The co-design approach reduces computational cost and yields effective masks for turbulence mitigation.

title: Optical Fourier Surfaces For Free-Space Computer-Generated Holography
authors: Y. M. Glauser, C. -Y. Shen, D. B. Seda, \c{c}. I\c{s}il, P. Benito Eberhard, H. Niese, J. G. Crimmann, D. Petter, G. Nagamine, S. J. W. Vonk, N. Lassaline, A. Ozcan, D. J. Norris
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-generated holography can shape electromagnetic fields by encoding wavefront information in nanostructured surfaces. However, despite significant progress, hologram designs for visible and near-infrared wavelengths remain largely limited by fabrication constraints. Most implementations rely on lithographic methods that produce discretized surfaces that do not match the wave nature of light. Further advances would benefit from accurate continuous (grayscale) control of interfacial profiles, which would allow straightforward design principles from Fourier optics to be applied. In this work, we introduce optical Fourier surfaces as a versatile, intuitive platform for free-space computer-generated holograms. Exploiting these arbitrarily wavy surfaces, we demonstrate three different design strategies for computer-generated holography. First, we use an analytical linear design approach based on sinusoidal lenses and gratings as fundamental holographic building blocks. Second, we enhance diffraction efficiencies through an iterative Fourier-transform algorithm. Finally, we extend our framework with machine-learning-based inverse design, creating wavelength-multiplexed holograms that reconstruct distinct diffraction responses in a predefined image plane. Our results combine advanced thermal scanning-probe lithography with flexible design strategies to create useful structures for photonic applications, particularly in settings where rapid prototyping is crucial.
tldr: This paper introduces optical Fourier surfaces for free-space computer-generated holography, focusing on fabrication and design strategies for visible and near-infrared wavelengths.
motivation: Current hologram designs are limited by fabrication constraints that produce discretized surfaces, and the authors aim to achieve accurate continuous control of interfacial profiles to apply Fourier optics principles.
method: The authors use thermal scanning-probe lithography to create arbitrarily wavy surfaces and demonstrate three design strategies: analytical linear design, iterative Fourier-transform algorithm, and machine-learning-based inverse design.
result: They demonstrate wavelength-multiplexed holograms that reconstruct distinct diffraction responses, combining advanced fabrication with flexible design strategies.
conclusion: Optical Fourier surfaces provide a versatile platform for computer-generated holography, particularly useful for rapid prototyping in photonic applications.

title: Scale-Bridging Phase-Field Modeling Of Microstructure Evolution By Fe$^2$ Computational Homogenization
authors: Geralf H\"utter, Fenil Lathiya, Vincent von Oertzen, Bjoern Kiefer
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-field models have become a standard tool for simulating complex microstructure evolution in materials, but their application to engineering-scale components is often hindered by prohibitive computational costs arising from the need to resolve fine-scale features. To address this challenge, we propose a consistent homogenization framework for phase-field theory. By enforcing a Hill-Mandel-type condition of micro-homogeneity formulated in terms of Gurtin's microforces, a well-posed boundary value problem is derived for the representative volume element (RVE), establishing rigorous micro-macro relations for both the order parameter and its gradient. The theory is implemented within a computational two-scale (FE[MATH]) scheme and validated against direct numerical simulations. Two distinct examples are investigated: a minimal Allen-Cahn model and a mechanically-coupled model for stress-driven martensitic phase transformation. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can reliably predict the spatial and temporal evolution of the macroscopically averaged fields with reasonable accuracy.
tldr: This paper proposes a computational homogenization framework for phase-field modeling of microstructure evolution, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Phase-field models are computationally expensive for engineering-scale components due to fine-scale resolution requirements. The authors aim to develop a consistent homogenization framework to bridge scales.
method: A Hill-Mandel-type micro-homogeneity condition is enforced using Gurtin's microforces, leading to a well-posed RVE boundary value problem. The theory is implemented in a computational two-scale FE² scheme.
result: The framework is validated on a minimal Allen-Cahn model and a mechanically-coupled martensitic phase transformation model, showing reliable prediction of macroscopically averaged fields.
conclusion: The proposed homogenization approach enables efficient phase-field simulations at engineering scales while maintaining accuracy for microstructure evolution.

title: Wireless Decentralized Federated Learning Via Device Clustering And Inter-Cluster Link Enhancement
authors: William Weijia Zheng, Hang Liu, Ying-Jun Angela Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) dispenses with the central server of classical FL by utilizing peer-to-peer model exchanges among edge devices. This server-free architecture enables ad-hoc, flexible distributed learning in large device-to-device (D2D) networks. However, wireless DFL converges slowly because peer-to-peer model aggregation incurs high delays and errors. Each DFL training round involves many-to-many gradient sharing over wireless channels, resulting in uncoordinated channel access, large communication errors from stragglers, and slow model consensus, especially in large-scale D2D networks with pronounced clustering structures. We address these aggregation bottlenecks by provisioning a few reliable backhaul links at straggling nodes to enhance network connectivity. Building on this idea, our budget-aware, cluster-centric DFL framework first partitions the network into densely connected clusters, and then allocates the limited backhaul budget to selected cluster heads. The resulting two-tier protocol executes fast, parallel model aggregation within clusters and infrequent inter-cluster exchanges among the heads, yielding an O(1/t) convergence rate in t iterations. Numerical experiments on image-classification tasks confirm that our approach accelerates convergence compared to state-of-the-art DFL baselines with only a few strategically placed backhaul links.
tldr: This paper proposes a wireless decentralized federated learning framework using device clustering and limited backhaul links to accelerate convergence.
motivation: Wireless DFL suffers from slow convergence due to high delays and errors in peer-to-peer model aggregation, especially in large-scale networks with clustering structures.
method: The framework partitions the network into densely connected clusters and allocates a limited backhaul budget to selected cluster heads, enabling fast intra-cluster aggregation and infrequent inter-cluster exchanges.
result: The proposed approach achieves an O(1/t) convergence rate and accelerates convergence on image-classification tasks compared to state-of-the-art DFL baselines.
conclusion: Strategically placing a few backhaul links can significantly improve wireless DFL performance without requiring full connectivity.

title: An Explicit Higher-Order Dual Basis For A Multiplicatively Calder\'on Preconditioned Electric Field Integral Equation
authors: Bernd Hofmann, Thomas F. Eibert, Francesco P. Andriulli, Simon B. Adrian
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the most effective means to precondition the electric field integral equation (EFIE) discretized with Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) functions is the multiplicative Calder\'on preconditioner employing Buffa-Christiansen (BC) functions as a basis dual to the RWG basis. It results in a formulation that is free from the dense-discretization and the low-frequency breakdown. To generalize the multiplicative Calder\'on preconditioner from the low-order BC and RWG basis to higher orders, we utilize B-spline-based basis functions and establish the first explicit high-order dual basis. It can be regarded as a generalization of the BC functions to arbitrary polynomial degrees and constitutes a fundamental building block for other approaches that rely on a dual basis. Numerical results for the obtained preconditioner demonstrate a low and constant number of generalized minimum residual (GMRES) iterations independent of the number of unknonws and the polynomial degree for canonical and realistic perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) scatterers; a key to enable the full potential of higher-order bases.
tldr: This paper presents a higher-order dual basis for the multiplicative Calderón preconditioner applied to the electric field integral equation, improving numerical stability for electromagnetic scattering problems.
motivation: The multiplicative Calderón preconditioner for the EFIE is limited to low-order basis functions; a higher-order dual basis is needed to extend its benefits to higher-order discretizations.
method: The authors construct an explicit higher-order dual basis using B-spline functions, generalizing the Buffa-Christiansen basis to arbitrary polynomial degrees, and integrate it into the multiplicative Calderón preconditioner.
result: Numerical experiments show that the preconditioner achieves a low and constant number of GMRES iterations independent of the number of unknowns and polynomial degree for canonical and realistic PEC scatterers.
conclusion: The proposed higher-order dual basis enables the full potential of higher-order bases in Calderón preconditioning, offering a robust solver for electromagnetic integral equations.

title: Another Look At The Static Pde Approach To Multidimensional Extrapolation
authors: Hwi Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a variant of the static PDE based extrapolation method (2014 Aslam, SIAM J. Sci. Comp) for extending smooth fields across interfaces implicitly defined as zero level sets. Our approach introduces the idea of relaxed upwinding finite differences as a key modification within the fast sweeping method. Unlike existing approaches, we require function values and their normal derivatives only on the first grid layer inside the domain adjacent to the boundary, thereby improving computational efficiency and flexibility. To further improve accuracy, we introduce a simple boundary reconstruction technique that significantly reduces the numerical error in the extrapolated solution near the boundary. Numerical experiments indicate enhanced performance of our approach across a range of domain geometries, including those with high curvature features.
tldr: This paper presents a variant of the static PDE-based extrapolation method for extending smooth fields across interfaces, using relaxed upwinding finite differences and a boundary reconstruction technique.
motivation: Existing static PDE extrapolation methods require function values and normal derivatives on multiple grid layers, which can be computationally inefficient and less flexible.
method: The authors introduce relaxed upwinding finite differences within the fast sweeping method, requiring data only on the first grid layer, and add a boundary reconstruction technique to reduce numerical error.
result: Numerical experiments show improved performance across various domain geometries, including those with high curvature features.
conclusion: The proposed variant enhances computational efficiency and accuracy for extrapolating smooth fields across implicitly defined interfaces.

title: Continuous Aperture Array-Assisted Integrated Communication And Navigation In Leo Satellite Constellations
authors: Qi Wang, Xiaoming Chen, Qiao Qi, Zhaolin Wang, Yuanwei Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a novel continuous aperture array (CAPA)-assisted integrated communication and navigation (ICAN) framework for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations. Within this framework, an electromagnetic-based collaborative transmission model is developed, in which multiple satellites equipped with CAPAs simultaneously radiate downlink data streams and navigation reference signals over shared spectrum. Building upon this, the achievable communication rate and the navigation Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) are derived, which explicitly characterize the intrinsic coupling between the dual-function beamformers and system performance. To improve the positioning accuracy with communication quality of service guarantee, a joint beamforming optimization problem is formulated to minimize the average CRB subject to transmit power budgets and minimum rate constraints. To tackle the inherent infinite-dimensionality of the CAPA beamformer design, an ICAN channel subspace is introduced to equivalently transform the formulation into a tractable finite-dimensional problem, which is then efficiently solved via an iterative convex optimization algorithm. Finally, numerical results demonstrate that the proposed CAPA-assisted beamforming design algorithm significantly outperforms conventional discrete phased array architectures and other benchmark schemes, yielding notable improvements in ICAN performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a continuous aperture array (CAPA)-assisted integrated communication and navigation framework for LEO satellite constellations, focusing on joint beamforming optimization to improve positioning accuracy under communication constraints.
motivation: To enhance both communication and navigation performance in LEO satellite systems by leveraging CAPA technology, which offers higher degrees of freedom than conventional phased arrays.
method: An electromagnetic-based collaborative transmission model is developed, and a joint beamforming optimization problem is formulated to minimize the average Cramer-Rao bound subject to power and rate constraints. The infinite-dimensional problem is transformed into a finite-dimensional one using an ICAN channel subspace and solved via iterative convex optimization.
result: Numerical results show that the proposed CAPA-assisted beamforming design significantly outperforms conventional discrete phased array architectures and other benchmarks in integrated communication and navigation performance.
conclusion: CAPA technology can substantially improve the trade-off between communication and navigation in LEO satellite constellations, offering a promising approach for future satellite systems.

title: Modeling And Analysis For Multiple-Layer Leo Satellite Internet Of Things Constellations
authors: Ming Ying, Xiaoming Chen, Qiao Qi, Yichao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To provide multiple-satellite coverage for global Internet of Things (IoT), a low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite IoT constellation usually contains multiple-layer orbits with different altitudes. However, the performance of multiple-layer LEO satellite IoT constellations under practical Rician fading satellite channels remains unknown due to complex theoretical modeling and intractable mathematical analysis. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a stochastic geometry-based modeling and analysis framework for multiple-layer LEO satellite IoT constellations, integrating Rician channel modeling and Cox point processes. Specifically, we introduce a novel channel approximation method to overcome the intractable expressions caused by the Rician fading. Building on this method, we derive exact closed-form expressions for key performance metrics, including connectivity probability, coverage probability, and transmission rate, especially in the case of IoT short-packet transmission. Extensive simulation results validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed model and reveal significant design insights. The results not only provide new theoretical perspectives for modeling and analysis of LEO satellite IoT constellations but also offer practical guidance for system deployment and optimization.
tldr: This paper proposes a stochastic geometry-based framework for modeling and analyzing multiple-layer LEO satellite IoT constellations under Rician fading channels.
motivation: The performance of multiple-layer LEO satellite IoT constellations under practical Rician fading is unknown due to complex modeling and analysis challenges.
method: The authors introduce a novel channel approximation method and derive closed-form expressions for connectivity, coverage, and transmission rate using Cox point processes.
result: Exact closed-form expressions for key performance metrics are derived and validated through simulations, revealing design insights for system deployment.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides new theoretical perspectives and practical guidance for LEO satellite IoT constellation design and optimization.

title: Nonexchangeable Logit Dynamics With Cost Constraints: Different Viewpoints And Numerical Analysis
authors: Tomohiro Tanaka Hidekazu Yoshioka
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The logit dynamic, a nonlinear dynamical system, subject to a const constraint with heterogeneous agents is formulated, and its well-posedness is studied from both agent-based (stochastic differential equation: SDE) and probabilistic (Fokker-Planck equation: FPE) viewpoints. The state space of agent actions is a compact domain in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The SDE is of the McKean-Vlasov type and is driven by jumps with finite variations, whereas the FPE is a nonlinear integro-differential equation. A key to our mathematical analysis of the FPE is adding a regularization factor into the cost constraint to mitigate the blow-up of the logit function. This property carries over to the McKean-Vlasov SDE. We also present a numerical method based on a na\"ive finite difference discretization for computing the FPE along with demonstrative computational examples, showing that the regularization method does not critically affect numerical solutions while preventing the breakdown of numerical computation. Finally, we conduct another demonstrative application study in which environmental, energy, and fishery resources intersect.
tldr: This paper studies logit dynamics with cost constraints from agent-based and probabilistic viewpoints, with numerical analysis.
motivation: To formulate and analyze a logit dynamic system with heterogeneous agents under cost constraints, ensuring well-posedness and numerical stability.
method: Uses McKean-Vlasov SDE with jumps and a nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation with a regularization factor to prevent blow-up, along with finite difference discretization.
result: The regularization method prevents numerical breakdown without critically affecting solutions; demonstrative examples in environmental, energy, and fishery resources are provided.
conclusion: The proposed regularization approach effectively stabilizes the logit dynamics model, enabling numerical computation for applications in resource management.

title: A Stabilizer Interpretation Of The Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller Group $\mathsf{GRT}_1(\mathbf K)$
authors: Hidekazu Furusho Benjamin Enriquez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: If [MATH] and [MATH] are Lie algebras, then the product [MATH] of their outer automorphism groups naturally acts on the set of outer Lie algebra morphisms from [MATH] to [MATH]; the stabilizer of the outer class of a given such morphism is then a subgroup of [MATH]. We show that this leads to two related interpretation of the Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group [MATH], where [MATH] are the Lie algebra of infinitesimal braids on the plane (resp. framed infinitesimal braids on the sphere) with 3 and 4 (resp. 4 and 5) strands: namely, it can be expressed as the joint intersection of the stabilizer groups of the outer classes of certain strand doubling morphisms [MATH] and [MATH] with [MATH], where [MATH] is a subgroup of [MATH] of outer classes of inertia-preserving automorphisms of [MATH].
tldr: This paper interprets the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group as stabilizers of outer Lie algebra morphisms related to braid Lie algebras.
motivation: To provide a new algebraic interpretation of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group using Lie algebras of infinitesimal braids.
method: The authors consider the action of outer automorphism groups on outer Lie algebra morphisms and show that the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group arises as the joint intersection of stabilizer groups of certain strand doubling morphisms.
result: The Grothendieck-Teichmüller group is expressed as the joint intersection of stabilizer groups of outer classes of strand doubling morphisms with a subgroup of inertia-preserving automorphisms.
conclusion: This offers a stabilizer interpretation of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group in terms of braid Lie algebras.

title: An Extension Of A Theorem Of Chevet
authors: Fabien Souli Olivier Gu\'edon (LAMA)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We adopt a modern approach to extend a comparison inequality of Chevet for Gaussian processes to a broader class of functions. Furthermore, we consider centered Gaussian random vectors associated with a family of [MATH] vectors on the unit sphere [MATH] and investigate configurations of the vertices for which these new functionals could be maximum for the regular simplex.
tldr: This paper extends a comparison inequality for Gaussian processes to a broader class of functions and studies configurations of vectors on the unit sphere.
motivation: To generalize Chevet's inequality for Gaussian processes and understand extremal configurations of spherical vectors.
method: Adopts a modern approach to extend the inequality and analyzes Gaussian random vectors on the sphere.
result: Provides an extension of Chevet's theorem and identifies conditions for the regular simplex to maximize certain functionals.
conclusion: The results contribute to geometric functional analysis and probability theory, but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Seed For Privacy -- Semi-automatic Privacy-revealing Data Reminder In Databases And Data Streams
authors: He Gu, Thomas Plagemann, Vera Goebel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sharing databases and data streams imposes the danger of revealing private information in the form of complex events which can comprise individual data elements and their combinations. Identifying these privacy-revealing complex events is crucial for preserving privacy while maintaining data utility. However, data producers often lack the expertise to comprehensively identify these events, which undermines many state-of-the-art privacy-preserving mechanisms that rely on accurate event labeling. To address this challenge, we developed pArborist - a tool that can semi-automatically create a set of queries to identify and label privacy-revealing complex events in both static datasets and dynamic data streams, guided by the privacy requirements of the data producer. pArborist uses the schema of the database or data stream combined with initial input from the data producer, i.e., seed queries. From each seed query, pArborist grows a tree containing all possible syntactically correct queries, constrained by an upper limit on computational resources. Following this growing phase, the tree is refined by eliminating queries that lack correlation to the seed or are conditionally independent of the seed.
